sharedFindings: The M307 eleven-family map remains accurate after M308-M318; no current evidence promotes Stage 11 or changes producer ownership.
The project-target session and packaged keyboard recovery now prove a safe review transport boundary, but they do not convert direct project-store commands into proposals.

Ordinary rename is the smallest content-independent mutating boundary: it changes workspace metadata, has an exact project target and workspace generation, and can be previewed without carrying Scene JSON or raw asset bytes.
Ordinary create/save/save-as are content-bearing and must retain atomic persistence, backup, directory-entry, asset-tree, generation, and foreign-state semantics outside generic history payloads.

Asset import/binding remains a separate boundary because candidate bytes and role-specific validation must remain outside ProposalBatch history; recovery restore/detach already has separate typed authority.
Add blank Scene is an in-memory editor mutation and should not implicitly save or share authority with project persistence until an explicit editor proposal boundary is accepted.

selectedNextSlice.name: metadata-only project-rename proposal preview and adapter
selectedNextSlice.scope: Add a pure typed preview/adapter boundary for one explicitly selected project display-name rename. Bind the exact project ID, current workspace index generation, current display name, proposed display name, stable project/content identity, and a deterministic preview hash into the generic local-project ProposalBatch envelope with human/no-provider provenance and one opaque allowlisted rename command. Keep workspace persistence execution, project content, raw bytes, credentials, providers, browser, Foundry, and desktop UI integration out of the slice.
selectedNextSlice.reason: Rename is the smallest ordinary mutating producer that does not require generic persistence of Scene JSON or asset bytes; isolating it first reduces the risk of collapsing project-store authority while establishing a reusable ordinary-producer preview shape.
